correctness.rationale: Two distinct standard-library exact-cover implementations generate 36 matchings and exhaust 36*2^10 matching-subset pairs; two logically equivalent forcing predicates agree on both coefficient vectors and the 6/30 frequencies. Different constructions of eight-cycle flips both produce 120 edges, a connected graph, diameter and radius three, and 6 degree-ten and 30 degree-six states. Exhaustiveness is argued from recursion branches and complete subset/pair enumeration. All program paths and outputs in the same package were run and inspected.

value.rationale: C20 is the smallest fullerene and a standard Kekulé matching test case. The known forcing spectrum is constant {3}, whereas the complete forcing-subset distributions distinguish two structurally meaningful classes and quantify identification redundancy across every subset size. The matching-class distinction coincides exactly with degree-ten versus degree-six mobility in the shortest alternating-even-cycle flip graph; its diameter and connectivity are exact and non-implied by forcing number or matching count.
